newsitem.title: USA: Miami commissioners approve deficit plan.
newsitem.headline: Miami commissioners approve deficit plan.

text.p: Miami city commissioners on Monday unanimously approved a plan to close the city's $68 million deficit through enhanced revenues, union concessions and spending reductions.
The plan was due to be submitted to the state's Financial Oversight Board, appointed to guide the city's recovery, by January 3.

By a 4-0 vote, commissioners approved a plan that would close the city's deficit through $20 million in new revenues, another $20 million in revenue enhancements, $10 million in expense reductions, $10 million in union concessions, $5 million in pension contributions and $5 million in cost containment measures.

City manager Edward Marquez said the plan provided for at least 60 percent of Miami's recurring deficit to be covered by recurring revenues or expense reductions and began to address the funding of operational and managerial shortcomings.

The measures would close the $68 million budget deficit discovered in the summer following the indictment of several city officials on corruption charges. The deficit represented nearly 25 percent of Miami's $275 million budget for the fiscal year that began October 1.
In December, Florida Governor Lawton Chiles declared a fiscal crisis and appointed a five-member oversight committee headed by Lt. Gov. Kenneth "Buddy" MacKay, to guide the city's recovery.
The city must present a five-year fiscal recovery plan to the committee by April.
